See http://ivyspring.com/terms for full terms and conditions. Rationale : Biomarkers for the diagnosis of heart failure (HF) are clinically essential. Circulating antimicrobial peptides LL-37 has emerged as a novel biomarker in cardiovascular disease, however, its relevance as a biomarker for acute HF are undetermined. Methods : Acute HF patients were enrolled in this study and the serum levels of LL-37/CRAMP (cathelicidin-related antimicrobial peptide) were measured by ELISA. The receiver-operator characteristic (ROC) curve was used to determine if serum LL-37 could be a biomarker for acute HF. Mouse CRAMP (mCRAMP, mouse homolog for human LL-37) was also determined in both heart and serum samples of, transverse aortic constriction (TAC)- and isoproterenol (ISO)-induced HF mice models, and phenylephrine (PE) and angiotensin II (AngII)-induced neonatal mouse cardiomyocytes (NMCMs) hypertrophic models, both intracellular and secreted, by ELISA. The protective effects of mCRAMP were determined in TAC, ISO, and AngII-induced HF in mice while whether HF was exacerbated in AngII-infused animals were checked in mCRAMP knockout mice. The underlying mechanism for protective effects of CARMP in pathological hypertrophy was determined by using a NF-κB agonist together with rCRAMP (rat homolog for human LL-37) in AngII or PE treated neonatal rat cardiomyocytes (NRCMs). Results : Serum levels of LL-37 were significantly decreased in acute HF patients (area under the curve (AUC) of 0.616), and negatively correlated with NT-proBNP. We further confirmed that mCRAMP was decreased in both heart and serum samples of TAC- and ISO-induced HF mice models. Moreover, in PE and AngII-induced NMCMs hypertrophic models, both intracellular and secreted mCRAMP levels were reduced. Functionally, mCRAMP could attenuate TAC, ISO, and AngII-induced HF in mice while CRAMP deficiency exacerbated HF. Mechanistically, the anti-hypertrophy effects of CRAMP were mediated by NF-κB signaling. Conclusions : Collectively, serum LL-37 is associated with acute HF and increasing CRAMP is protective against deleterious NF-κB signaling in the rodent. Cathelicidin CRAMP LL-37 Heart Failure Serum Biomarker NF-κB Introduction Heart failure (HF) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide 1 , 2 . HF is the final stage upon different initial cardiac insults, affecting over 1% of people aged over 50 years and increases progressively with age 3 . Hereby HF remains a major health epidemic, causing significant economic and public heath burdens in the world 1 . Despite great advances in the treatment of HF, HF patients still have a poor prognosis, with high rates of hospital readmission and mortality 4 , 5 . Moreover, especially for acute HF, no new therapies have improved clinical outcomes and admissions continue to increase and novel biomarkers and effective therapies are highly needed 1 , 6 , 7 . Cathelicidin-related antimicrobial peptide (CRAMP) is the rodent form of LL-37 in human 8 . CRAMP can be expressed by many cells, including neutrophils, monocytes, macrophages, corneal fibroblasts, epithelial cells, B lymphocytes, T lymphocytes, NK cells, and mast cells 9 , 10 . Besides a direct antimicrobial activity and immunomodulation effects, CRAMP has many other functional roles, including would healing, chemoattraction, cell proliferation, cell migration, apoptosis, epithelial-mesenchymal-transition, angiogenesis, and inflammation 8 , 11 - 14 . Changes of CRAMP levels have been linked to cancer and a variety of autoimmune diseases, including systemic lupus erythematous, arthritis, pancreatitis, and atherosclerosis 8 , 15 - 20 . We also reported that CRAMP, produced by pancreatic ß-cells, could attenuate autoimmune-induced diabetes by affecting regulatory immune cells in the pancreas 21 . In the cardiovascular system, CRAMP has been found to be able to protect against cardiac fibrosis in diabetic mice 22 . Besides, we and other groups have reported that CRAMP could protect against myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury and enhance bone marrow cell retention in the treatment of cardiac dysfunction induced by myocardial infarction 9 , 23 . Recently, CRAMP was shown to suppress cardiac hypertrophy upon induction via pressure overload 24 . However, it is unclear if CRAMP can be used as a treatment for different causes of HF. Besides, circulating CRAMP has emerged as a biomarker of different cardiovascular disease 9 , 25 , but the functional role of circulating CRAMP in HF remains to be delineated. In the present study, we investigated if circulating LL-37/CRAMP could be a biomarker for acute HF and determined whether it can be used as a therapy for different HF backgrounds. We observed that serum LL-37 levels were significantly decreased in acute HF patients and were negatively correlated with NT-proBNP. In addition, we found that CRAMP was decreased in both heart and serum samples in transverse aortic constriction (TAC) and isoproterenol (ISO)-induced rodent HF models, and in neonatal mouse cardiomyocytes (NMCMs) cell hypertrophy models induced by phenylephrine (PE) and angiotensin II (AngII). Most importantly, CRAMP could attenuate multiple mice models of HF. In vitro , we proved evidence that the inhibition of NF-κB signaling contributed to the anti-hypertrophy effects of CRAMP. These findings suggest that serum CRAMP not only have a potential as a biomarker of acute HF, but also that increasing CRAMP is protective for HF induced by multiple types of cardiac stresses.

extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigated LL-37/CRAMP as both a potential biomarker and therapeutic agent for acute heart failure (HF) and cardiac hypertrophy. It revealed that serum LL-37/CRAMP levels are significantly decreased in acute HF patients and various preclinical models of HF. Functionally, therapeutic administration of CRAMP was found to attenuate HF and pathological hypertrophy in these models. Mechanistically, CRAMP's cardioprotective effects against hypertrophy were mediated through the inhibition of NF-κB signaling, highlighting its dual potential as a diagnostic biomarker and a protective therapeutic target for acute HF.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The primary therapeutic method involved administration of cathelicidin-related antimicrobial peptides (CRAMP, mCRAMP, rCRAMP). Heart failure and hypertrophy models were induced using Transverse Aortic Constriction (TAC) surgery, Angiotensin II (Ang II) infusion, Isoproterenol (ISO) infusion, and Phenylephrine (PE) treatment.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: CRAMP treatments included mCRAMP peptide supplementation for 2 or 4 weeks in mice, and 0.1 mg/L for 48 h in cardiomyocytes. rCRAMP was applied to neonatal rat cardiomyocytes. Inducers for HF models included Ang II (1.3 mg/kg/day for 4 weeks in mice; 1 µM for 48 h in cardiomyocytes), Isoproterenol (30 mg/kg/day for 2 weeks in mice), and PE (100 µM for 48 h in cardiomyocytes). TAC surgery involved tying a 27-gauge needle parallel to the transverse aorta with 7-0 silk suture. Betulinic acid (BA) was used at 20 µM for 48 h in cardiomyocytes. Generally, no explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for the various treatments, beyond the duration of supplementation.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly decreased in acute HF patients (AUC 0.616, P<0.001; 90.59% specificity, 29.03% sensitivity), negatively correlated with NT-proBNP (R=-0.174, P=0.030), with a cutoff of 1203.525 pg/ml. Also decreased in saliva from NYHA class I/II HF patients.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Human cathelicidin peptide (analogue of CRAMP) involved in antimicrobial activity, immunomodulation, wound healing, chemoattraction, cell proliferation, cell migration, apoptosis, epithelial-mesenchymal-transition, angiogenesis, inflammation, innate/adaptive immune response, and potential cardiac protection.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Acute Heart Failure (HF) patients, NYHA class I/II HF patients.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential novel diagnostic biomarker for acute HF; decreased circulating levels are associated with acute HF and observed in early-stage HF patients.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Mouse heart tissue, mouse serum, neonatal mouse cardiomyocytes (NMCMs) (intracellular and secreted), systemic (in mCRAMP knockout mice)
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Protein Level, Protein Level (therapeutic elevation), Protein Level (genetic reduction/absence)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased in heart and serum of TAC- and ISO-induced HF mice. Reduced intracellular and secreted levels in PE- and AngII-induced NMCMs hypertrophic models. Therapeutic administration of mCRAMP attenuated TAC, ISO, and AngII-induced HF in mice. CRAMP deficiency (knockout) exacerbated AngII-induced HF.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Rodent homolog of human LL-37, a cathelicidin-related antimicrobial peptide. Functions include antimicrobial activity, immunomodulation, wound healing, chemoattraction, cell proliferation, cell migration, apoptosis, epithelial-mesenchymal-transition, angiogenesis, inflammation. Crucially, it protects against cardiac fibrosis, myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury, enhances bone marrow cell retention, and suppresses cardiac hypertrophy, primarily through inhibition of NF-κB signaling.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Transverse aortic constriction (TAC)-induced HF, Isoproterenol (ISO)-induced HF, Angiotensin II (AngII)-induced HF/hypertrophy (in vivo and in vitro), Phenylephrine (PE)-induced hypertrophy (in vitro), CRAMP deficiency models.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Endogenous levels are associated with and indicative of heart failure and cardiac hypertrophy. Increasing mCRAMP/CRAMP is protective against heart failure and cardiac hypertrophy, while its deficiency exacerbates HF. Has potential as a therapeutic agent.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Levels ≥ 1,000 pg/mL used as a diagnostic criterion for acute HF. Negatively correlated with serum LL-37 levels (R=-0.174, P=0.030).
